verdict.rationale: Teller is API-first, and its core data and money-movement functions are exposed as documented API resources: live balances, transactions, identity and Zelle payments. However, webhook registration is documented only through the Teller Dashboard, and no OpenAPI spec was found, so API parity with the UI is not established. Missing for 10: evidence that dashboard functions (webhook configuration, certificate/application management) are available via API, any documented parity claim, a machine-readable API spec, and independent corroboration of full API coverage.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: The account balances API provides your application with live, real-time account balances.
The transactions API exposes the ledger transactions of a financial account.
The payments resource allows you to send payments to yourself or a 3rd party on behalf of the end-user from their account.
You can configure a new webhook from the Teller Dashboard
